The 9th ASEAN Ministerial Meeting on Drug Matters (AMMD) was convened via videoconference on 15 October 2026. The Meetings brought together AMMD Leaders from all ASEAN Member States. The Deputy Secretary-General of ASEAN for ASEAN Political-Security Community, H.E. Dato’ Astanah Abdul Aziz, represented the ASEAN Secretariat at the Meeting. The AMMD, which is convened biennially, exchanged views on the evolving illicit drug situation in the region and discussed ways to further strengthen ASEAN’s collective response to these challenges. The 9th AMMD also discussed the outcomes of the 47th ASEAN Senior Officials Meeting on Drug Matters (ASOD) and Its Related Meetings held in August 2026, as well as updates on the Final Review of the ASEAN Work Plan on Securing Communities Against Illicit Drugs 2016-2025. The Meeting also adopted the Concept Note on Updating Annex I of the ASEAN Charter on the Nomenclature of ASOD to read as “ASEAN Senior Officials Meeting on Drug Matters” and the Guidelines of Practices and Protocols for the AMMD and Its Subsidiary Mechanisms. The ASEAN Secretariat briefed the Meeting on recent developments in ASEAN. The Meeting was preceded by the Preparatory ASOD for the 9th AMMD, held via videoconference on 14 October 2026.

Deputy Secretary-General of ASEAN for ASEAN Political-Security Community, H.E. Dato’ Astanah Abdul Aziz, met with the Deputy Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Hellenic Republic, H.E. Theoharis Theoharis, on 13 October 2026. They exchanged views on ways to further enhance relations between ASEAN and Hellenic Republic, and discussed opportunities to advance cooperation in areas of common interest, particularly trade and investment. Prior to the Meeting, Deputy Minister Theoharis gifted a statue titled “The Daughter of Ephthidicos” to the ASEAN Secretariat.

Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, on 14 October 2026 attended a working dinner with members of the ASEAN Committee in Moscow (ACM), on the margins of his working visit to Russia. The engagement provided an opportunity for Dr. Kao to exchange views with the ACM on ASEAN's current priorities, the latest developments in ASEAN-Russia relations, and the role of the ACM in promoting ASEAN's interests and visibility in Russia.

1. Bengaluru does not have an IIT of its own. But it is home to more than 50,000 IIT alumni—and now, a centre that is trying to bring all 23 IITs together under one roof. 2. The IIT Alumni Centre Bengaluru, or IITACB, serves as a platform that links the IIT ecosystem with industry players and the government. Firms bring their “pain points” to the centre, which then circulates those among 23 IITs for solutions. 3. IITACB does not get involved in the technical details or commercial agreement between the company and the IIT. Its role is to widen the pool of expertise available to both sides. It essentially works as “a facilitator or matchmaker.” 4. Take Tathyakosh for example. It’s a public-data discovery platform launched by ACSEL Technology Forum in collaboration with IITACB. It brings over 1.5 million public datasets onto one searchable platform. 5. A startup, which built an AI model to automate health-risk assessments for insurance firms, not only benefited from the mentorship but also raised Rs 1 crore in funding. Now, footage from May to September shows just how far he's come, with Loustaunau saying he's regained nearly all his functionality. Video

هیأت معاونت سازمان ملل متحد در افغانستان (یوناما) در گزارش سه‌ماهه خود، در باره وضعیت حقوق بشری، از اول جولای تا ۳۰ سپتمبر ۲۰۲۶، از ادامه محدودیت‌ها بر زنان، تلفات غیرنظامیان و محدودیت‌ها بر رسانه‌ها خبر داده است. بر بنیاد این گزارش، بیش از ۵۰ مورد بازداشت و هشدار به زنان به‌دلیل رعایت‌نکردن حجاب، مجازات بدنی، بازداشت خودسرانه ثبت شده است. یوناما همچنان از کشته‌شدن ۱۳ غیرنظامی و زخمی‌شدن ۲۰ نفر دیگر در "رویدادهای مرزی" خبر داده است. در این گزارش به ادامه محرومیت دختران از آموزش، محدودیت‌های کار و رفت‌وآمد زنان، ممنوعیت ورود کارمندان زن افغان به دفترهای سازمان ملل، نیز اشاره شده است. یوناما همچنان از توقف فعالیت برخی رسانه‌ها، بازداشت خبرنگاران، لغو جواز دانشگاه خاتم‌النبیین، بسته‌شدن نهادهای وابسته به جامعه شیعه، نشر قانون جدید پولیس و بازنگری قوانین برای مطابقت با شریعت اسلامی گزارش داده است. مگر امارت‌اسلامی تا اکنون در واکنش به این گزارش چیزی نگفته است. #طلوع‌نیوز

Some things you should know about shipping traffic in the Black Sea: 1. Most ships headed to Ukraine or Russia are not accurately reporting their locations/destinations. Not even after they have left the Black Sea. That information is dangerous and both sides have access to folks that are good at tracking ships. This has broadly been the case for more than a year and was wide spread for Ukraine bound ships since the BSGI collapsed. 2. Reported locations should be fact checked with satellites as often there may be security or political reasons not to be accurate in reporting them. 3. Ownership and management data is not always accurate, again for security reasons. 4. Often ships who sail the Black Sea have operated in these ports for a decade or more. Many of the ships that trade with Russia have previously traded with Ukraine, even since the full-scale invasion. Often Türkiye will be a transfer point for goods from both countries. 5. Broadly what we are seeing is area denial in the most important shipping lanes to restrict traffic to both Ukraine and Russia. As traffic flows change and ships take more active steps to hide their actions, the degree to which ‘general area’ vs ‘targeted ships’ matters when choosing targets is less important to the war aims. Russia especially is unconcerned with how their actions impact shipping traffic to Western Black Sea nations. One might even go so far as to believe reduced traffic to these nations is helpful to Russia’s overall strategy.

40 yrs ago, Iranians were victims of chemical weapons while the world watched. On Feb 28, Lamerd became a testing ground for new barbaric weapons. We must ensure that those who committed this war crime—& those who knowingly enabled them—are brought to justice #JusticeForLamerd Reza Nasri (@RezaNasri1) Today, I stood in Lamerd. I had read the reports. I had studied the forensic reconstructions by Airwars, The New York Times, BBC Verify, the painstaking work on trajectory angles, fragmentation patterns and blast radii. None of it prepared me for standing beneath these walls, or meeting the people who live behind them. Lamerd is a small city of about 30,000 people in Fars province. It is the kind of place where a stranger is offered food before anyone asks his name. I have rarely encountered a community so instinctively and openly hospitable. People who had only recently buried their children still insisted on pouring us tea. That warmth, in the face of what was done to them, is the first thing the world should know about Lamerd. The second is what these walls tell you, if you take the time to look. On February 28, 2026, the opening day of the US-Israeli war on Iran, the United States fired Precision Strike Missiles into this city. Independent forensic reconstruction has identified at least three. Eye witnesses say there were four. The PrSM is not an ordinary missile. It does not simply strike a point on the ground. It detonates in the air, roughly fifteen to twenty metres above the surface, turning the area beneath it into a killing zone. The blast sends tens of thousands of white-hot tungsten fragments in every direction, ripping through walls, cars and human bodies. Investigators counted more than 2,000 individual fragment impacts along a single 150-metre stretch of one residential street. I walked that street today. I did not need the number. I could see it. Look at the photographs. The facades are not simply damaged. They are pocked from roofline to foundation, in a pattern no accident could produce. The asphalt of the schoolyard is covered with hundreds of small grey scars where fragments struck the pavement. Then there is the steel door. The kind of door you would find on any modest home. It has been punched through in a dozen places. Taped above the holes is a photograph of a curly-haired toddler. Her name was Avina Barzegar. She was two years old. She was killed in her family's backyard. This is how the attack was described to us by people who lived through it. A missile struck first, directly above the Shahid Naimi sports hall, where a girls' volleyball team was training. Panic followed. People did what people instinctively do when something explodes nearby: they ran outside, toward the open air, believing that was where they might be safe. That was when the second missile came down. Then a third. Then a fourth. Each detonated over a different part of the same small city: a school, a residential area, places where people had run because they thought the street was safer than the building they had been inside. At least 21 civilians were killed that day, including children as young as two. More than 170 were wounded. Spinal injuries. Amputations. Catastrophic burns. We met the family of a seventeen-year-old girl who lost both eyes. We met the family of another young girl who will spend the rest of her life in a wheelchair, her spine severed by fragments that fell from a clear afternoon sky. I heard about a little girl who no longer speaks. The trauma and bleeding in her brain took her voice, along with so much of what childhood was supposed to give her. None of these girls carried a rifle. None wore a uniform. Among those killed and maimed in Lamerd, there was not a single member of an armed force, Iranian or otherwise. According to the forensic reconstruction, the missiles were launched from mobile batteries in a Persian Gulf Arab state that hosts American forces, a state that would later condemn Iran when Iran exercised its inherent right of self-defense. And what was Washington's response? It was not that Lamerd contained a military target. No such target has ever been identified by CENTCOM. Instead, the story changed. First, a CENTCOM spokesman flatly said that no American strike had taken place within thirty miles of Lamerd that day. Then footage emerged that could no longer be dismissed. The explanation changed. The missile seen in the footage, they said, was actually an Iranian Hoveyzeh cruise missile. Weapons analysts at Janes and McKenzie Intelligence, along with the visual-forensics teams at The New York Times and BBC Verify, examined the same footage independently. They reached the same conclusion. The silhouette, the mid-air detonation and the fragmentation pattern all pointed to one weapon used in that theater. It was not Iranian. None of this should surprise anyone who has followed this war closely. The PrSM had never been used in combat before February 28. Lamerd was its combat debut. A live-fire demonstration in a civilian city, whose geography apparently made it a convenient proving ground. And by the Pentagon's own measure, the test was a success. Within a month, Lockheed Martin had reached a new agreement with the Department of War to quadruple PrSM production, later reported by independent investigators to be worth some $8.4 billion. Days after the missile killed Avina Barzegar, CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper publicly celebrated its combat debut, calling it "an unrivaled deep strike capability." Tell that to the toddler on the door. Iranian civil society will not allow what happened in Lamerd to disappear the way so much of Iraq and Afghanistan disappeared from public memory. Those societies had their bar associations, universities and forensic institutions hollowed out by decades of dictatorship, invasion and war before anyone expected them to build a serious case file. Iran does not face those same constraints. It has tens of thousands of practicing lawyers, a functioning forensic medicine system, land and hospital registries, dozens of law faculties, and a diaspora that includes lawyers admitted to practice in jurisdictions that recognize universal jurisdiction. We will use every one of them. We will pursue Donald Trump, Marco Rubio, Pete Hegseth, Adm. Brad Cooper, and every officer who executed their orders, in every forum on this earth that will hear us, for as long as it takes. This is not only Iran's fight. People anywhere, including in the United States and Europe, can do something about it. 1- Pursue universal jurisdiction. If you live in a country that recognizes universal jurisdiction over grave breaches of the Geneva Conventions, press prosecutors to open a file. Many of these governments speak constantly about the independence of their judiciaries. This is where that claim gets tested. The legal basis exists. The precedents exist. 2- Demand an end to the contracts: Demand that your government, and any government with a Lockheed Martin contract, cancel it. Every state party to the Geneva Conventions has obligations to "ensure respect" for international humanitarian law. Those obligations do not disappear because a weapons contract is profitable. A company should not be able to field-test a weapon on a residential street and then collect billions of dollars to manufacture more of it. 3- Say their names. Be loud. Organize. Say Avina Barzegar's name. Say the names of the other children killed on that street. Keep saying them until they cannot be forgotten. Let Lamerd become the case that finally forces the world to confront this weapon and ban its use against civilians, so that no city anywhere becomes someone else's proving ground again. And do not accept, for one second, the claim that this is "still under investigation." This is a government that has told the American public that it can read an Iranian officer's name tag from a satellite in orbit. It closed the Lamerd file within days, through denial, without answering the questions raised by BBC Verify, The New York Times or Airwars. An administration with that level of claimed surveillance capability does not need more time to determine who fired four missiles into a city of 30,000 people. It has known since the morning of February 28. It has decided that the truth is inconvenient. Avina Barzegar was two years old. That is why we do not stop. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/RezaNasri1/status/2098781595360518197#m

Today, I held a series of bilateral discussions with Member States and development finance institutions, focused on deepening cooperation, expanding investment opportunities and translating shared priorities into concrete results for rural communities. I met with Jeremy Wiggins of the U.S. Department of the Treasury, Nguyen Quoc Phuong, Director General at Viet Nams Ministry of Finance and Liao Min, China's Vice Minister of Finance. These discussions are important to deepening our engagement with Member States and identifying opportunities for stronger collaboration. I also met Dr. Abdulhamid Alkhalifa, President of @TheOPECFund , and Michael Jongeneel, CEO of @FMO_development, to explore closer cooperation on development finance, private-sector investment and market creation, particularly in fragile contexts. A key milestone was signing a new cooperation and co-financing agreement with @isdb_group, alongside its President, Dr. Muhammad Sulaiman Al Jasser. This provides an important foundation for expanding joint investments, strengthening institutional cooperation and bringing our complementary expertise together. I also welcomed partners from the @arabcoordgroup for an exchange on how we can strengthen coordination, identify shared priorities and deliver greater collective impact. By working more closely across governments, international financial institutions and development banks, we can turn shared priorities into coordinated action and greater impact for rural communities on the ground. #FinancingTheFirstMile | #WBGMeetings | @IFAD

This morning, I hosted an #IFAD14 Asia and the Pacific Ministerial Roundtable, together with the Government of the Philippines on the margins of the @WorldBankGroup and @IMFNews Annual Meetings in Bangkok. I was pleased to welcome Ministers and representatives from Bangladesh, Bhutan, Nepal, Viet Nam, Samoa, Solomon Islands and Kiribati among others. The strong participation of Pacific Island countries was particularly important, highlighting the need for greater investment in resilient rural economies. The challenges are significant. Some countries in the region import over 85% of their fertilizer, while most Pacific small island developing states depend on imports for more than 60% of their food. Global supply chain disruptions and rising costs directly affect farmers, rural businesses and food security. Yet the opportunities are equally significant. Asia and the Pacific is @IFAD's largest regional portfolio, with deep domestic capital markets, dynamic private sectors and innovative financing models. From mobilizing private co-financing for rural enterprises in Bangladesh to strengthening agricultural value chains in the Philippines, targeted public investment can reduce risks and unlock additional capital. #FinancingTheFirstMile | #WBGMeetings | @IFADAsia

SpaceX uses ARGON ION PROPULSION to move Starlink satellites through space And the engineering is pretty wild Starlink satellites use argon Hall-effect thrusters electric engines that ionize argon gas and accelerate the charged particles at extremely high speed They allow Starlink satellites to: • Raise themselves into operational orbit • Maneuver around other spacecraft and debris • Maintain their position in space • Deorbit themselves at the end of their life SpaceX originally used krypton, but switched its next-generation Starlink satellites to argon The V2 Mini argon thruster produces: • 170 mN of thrust • 2.4X the thrust of the first-generation system • 1.5X the specific impulse And Starlink became the first spacecraft system to fly using argon propulsion in space A Falcon 9 gets Starlink into space Then these tiny electric engines keep thousands of satellites exactly where they need to be

The Trump administration imposed financial sanctions this month on the International Criminal Court, escalating a previously announced diplomatic campaign to “dismantle” the court. The sanctions prohibit U.S. companies and entities from transacting with the ICC. The Hague-based ICC seeks to investigate and prosecute those responsible for grave offenses such as genocide, crimes against humanity, and war crimes. It has 125 members, though dozens of governments are not parties to it, including China, India, Israel, Russia, and the United States. The court condemned the sanctions as an attempt to obstruct justice and intimidate those who work or cooperate with it, while foreign ministers from 8 U.S. allies released a joint statement expressing their disagreement with the U.S. decision. During the visit of Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Al Busaidi for the 8th Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission (JMC), Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif @CMShehbaz witnessed the exchange of six agreements and MoUs. Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 and Omani Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Al Busaidi signed the Protocol Recording the Minutes of the 8th Pakistan-Oman JMC, the Agreement on Mutual Visa Exemption for Holders of Diplomatic, Special, Official and Service Passports, and the MoU on Records and Archives. The remaining three MoUs, covering cooperation in information and broadcasting, IT and telecommunications, and news exchange and media cooperation, were signed by the Federal Minister for Information and Broadcasting and the Federal Minister for IT and Telecommunication, respectively. These exchanges reflect the shared commitment of Pakistan and Oman to expand cooperation across diverse sectors and further strengthen their longstanding bilateral relations.

Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar @MIshaqDar50 held a meeting with Mr. Vladimir Kolokoltsev, Interior Minister of the Russian Federation, at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs today. Federal Minister for Interior Mohsin Naqvi and Minister of State for Interior Talal Chaudhry also joined the meeting. The DPM/FM expressed satisfaction at the positive momentum in Pakistan–Russia relations, welcoming recent high-level visits and exchanges. The two sides discussed avenues for enhancing cooperation in trade, investment, culture and tourism, strengthening people-to-people ties, and maintaining close cooperation at multilateral fora, including the SCO.

Addressed the gathering at the launch of IIT Kanpur’s ‘Greater Than Us’ fundraising campaign in New Delhi. The purpose of a great institution is to serve something larger than any individual or generation. The knowledge it creates, the talent it nurtures and the opportunities it opens must ultimately contribute to society and to the nation. Supporting IIT Kanpur is therefore not simply an investment in an institution; it is an investment in possibilities that extend far beyond ourselves. Such an undertaking cannot be realised by the Institute alone. IIT Kanpur's distinguished alumni have carried its values into industry, entrepreneurship, academia, public service and many other fields. Their contribution can go beyond financial support to include mentoring, professional networks, research partnerships and opportunities for young people. Industry, philanthropic supporters and institutional partners also have an important role to play. When academia, government, industry and philanthropy work towards a shared purpose, research can find pathways to application, promising ideas can attract support, and talent can find opportunities to flourish. I congratulate everyone who has contributed to conceiving and advancing this Campaign. A Dublin hotel canceled a reservation for 70 rooms for delegates attending an international conference on combating antisemitism after learning the purpose of their visit, according to a senior representative of Ireland’s Jewish community. Maurice Cohen, chairman of the Jewish Representative Council of Ireland, disclosed the incident at a reception at the Irish Foreign Ministry Tuesday night marking the opening of a meeting of the Special Envoys and Coordinators Combating Antisemitism (SECCA), a group supported by the World Jewish Congress and the European Commission. “There is an uncomfortable irony in organizing an international conference to discuss antisemitism and finding that, before the conference has even begun, you have already encountered something that forces you to ask exactly the questions the conference was created to address,” Cohen said. “How quickly does the word ‘Jewish’ change a conversation? How easily does a gathering about antisemitism become associated with the Israeli army?” Read more on The Times of Israel.

Ramdin - OAS Secretary General (@SG_OEA_OAS) Artificial intelligence alone will not create prosperity. El Niño is leaving its fingerprint on the ocean—and ISRO’s satellite is watching! ISRO’s EOS-06 (Oceansat-3) is detecting a reduction in ocean Chlorophyll-a for the month of June 2026, indicating changes in tiny marine plants (phytoplankton), along with a shift in surface winds. From space, these changes offer a fascinating glimpse into the evolving 2026 El Niño and its impact on our oceans compared with signatures in 2024 & 2025. More information is available at the nices.nrsc.gov.in/apps/enso/ #ElNino #ISRO #Oceansat3 #EOS06 #OceanFromSpace #ClimateChange

Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif witnessed a ceremony of exchange of MoUs between Pakistan and the Sultanate of Oman, in Islamabad, today.
Foreign Minister of Oman H.E. Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Albusaidi called on Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif in Islamabad, today.

Prime Minister Muhammad Shehbaz Sharif received today the Foreign Minister of Oman, H.E. Sayyid Badr bin Hamad bin Hamood Albusaidi, who is on a visit to Pakistan to co-chair the 8th Session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission along with Deputy Prime Minister/Foreign Minister Senator Mohammad Ishaq Dar. Welcoming Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr, the Prime Minister highlighted that the strong bond of shared faith, geography, history, culture, and centuries of people-to- people exchanges between Pakistan and Oman provided a strong fraternal foundation to the bilateral relationship. He underscored that Pakistan considered Oman as a brotherly country, an important maritime neighbour and a valuable partner in a critically important region. The Prime Minister expressed satisfaction over the successful convening of the 8th Session of the Pakistan–Oman Joint Ministerial Commission. He hoped that the meeting would provide a strong foundation for further expanding mutually beneficial cooperation and deepening engagement between the two brotherly countries. The Prime Minister noted with deep satisfaction the unanimity of views between Pakistan and Oman on all regional and global issues. He appreciated Oman's principled stance of dialogue and diplomacy in resolving disputes. Foreign Minister Sayyid Badr thanked the Government of Pakistan for the hospitality extended to him and his delegation. He expressed satisfaction on successful holding of the 8th JMC Session and agreed that it would pave the way for enhanced bilateral collaboration in diverse sectors for mutual benefit. The Omani Foreign Minister also appreciated Pakistan's sustained diplomatic efforts towards de-escalating tensions and advancing peaceful solutions to regional challenges. The Prime Minister also witnessed the signing of the Protocol of the 8th Session of the Pakistan-Oman Joint Ministerial Commission, as well as the Agreements/MoU covering bilateral cooperation in the domains of media cooperation; news & information exchange; historical documentation & archives management; communication & information technology; as well as facilitation of diplomatic and official exchanges. Ambassador Petr Kopřiva presented his Letter of Credence to the Secretary-General of ASEAN, Dr. Kao Kim Hourn, at the ASEAN Headquarters/ASEAN Secretariat on 9 October 2026, officially assuming his role as Ambassador of the Czech Republic to ASEAN. Secretary-General Dr. Kao congratulated Ambassador Kopřiva on his appointment and reaffirmed the ASEAN Secretariat’s readiness to work closely with him and the Embassy of the Czech Republic in Jakarta to explore cooperation with ASEAN, both bilaterally and through the ASEAN-European Union (EU) Strategic Partnership framework, in areas of mutual interest. Both sides noted that the 50th anniversary of ASEAN-EU Dialogue Relations next year would provide an opportunity to further strengthen the partnership. Ambassador Kopřiva reaffirmed the Czech Republic’s commitment to deepening its relations with ASEAN and its Member States, as reflected in its Strategy for Cooperation with the Indo-Pacific, adopted in 2022. The commitment was also demonstrated by the participation of H.E. Petr Macinka, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs of the Czech Republic, at the 25th ASEAN-EU Ministerial Meeting (AEMM) held in Brunei Darussalam, in April 2026. Secretary-General Dr. Kao also encouraged Ambassador Kopřiva to engage with the Committee of Permanent Representatives to ASEAN and the wider diplomatic community in Jakarta, as well as to explore cooperation with relevant ASEAN centres of excellence. The Czech Republic appointed its first Ambassador to ASEAN in 2012. Ambassador Kopřiva succeeds Ambassador Jaroslav Doleček, who completed his tenure on 30 October 2025. Video

1. An isolated Saudi Arabia is fighting Houthis on its own soil & in Yemen. On Tuesday, the Saudi-backed coalition forces launched strikes on Houthi targets in Sanaa. #CutTheClutter looks at the limitations of Saudi Arabia, how its geography adds to the country’s vulnerability, & explains how and why military spending doesn’t guarantee security. 2. I use the word isolated deliberately. Saudi Arabia is a vast country, with a very small population concentrated in tiny urban & economic clusters. And between these pockets lie enormous stretches of desert where its critical infra is scattered. All of this provides the adversary with thousands of targets. Even if 1 missile gets through, it causes damage. Besides loss of life & property, it damages Saudi Arabia’s credibility. 3. Saudi Arabia & the ‘state’ it’s fighting — North Yemen — is an example of classical asymmetric warfare. Saudi Arabia is a super-rich, well-organised country but they are fighting a force that has nothing to lose. It is entirely amorphous, with no clear leadership structures or infrastructure nodes that the Saudis with their superior firepower could decapitate. 4. The other problem is Saudi Arabia’s main ally, the US, is distracted. Pakistan & Turkey have limitations. Are they going to put troops on the ground? Who will they fight? Also, do the Saudis really want Erdogan to send 100,000 troops in? Because what’s the guarantee he will then withdraw those? Gulf states may want Saudi Arabia to survive, but they also have vulnerable infra of their own. 5. So, what options do the Saudis have? · Escalate, but its Yemen campaign of 2015-22 shows the limits of force. · Create a more integrated regional defence structure. Question is everybody will unite, but will they come to fight? · Negotiate with the Houthis, offer them money. They will take it, but will also want recognition. Will Saudis be able to persuade others, including the US & Israel? · Rethink the Saudi security doctrine. They’ve got the shiny, imported arsenal, now Saudi Arabia will have to think of producing its own weaponry. #CutTheClutter with me, episode 1917: Loneliness of Saudi Arabia despite enormous defence spending as the isolated country fights Houthis ￼ youtube.com/watch?v=DLqCjvjX…

Can genetic data from Indian cancer patients help researchers develop a vaccine tailored to their tumours? At IIT Madras, a decade of cancer tissue collection and genomic research has laid the groundwork for an experimental mRNA breast cancer vaccine. (1/4) The National Cancer Tissue Biobank, set up at IIT Madras in 2015, was established to address the shortage of Indian cancer samples for research. It has since collected around 10,000 tissue samples from more than 12 hospitals, giving researchers material to study the genetic changes associated with cancer. (2/4) The team has identified tumour antigens reported to be unique to Indian patients, along with other potential targets. The vaccine is designed to use mRNA to help the body recognise these targets and mount an immune response against cancer cells. (3/4) Researchers are completing the vaccine construct and preparing to test it in a mouse model of breast cancer. What's inside IIT Madras' decade-long effort to develop a breast cancer vaccine tailored to Indian patients? (4/4) Read the full story by @RichhariyaSneha theprint.in/health/the-searc…

Unlocking market opportunities enables rural communities to increase incomes and reduce poverty. Stronger links with agroenterprises open pathways to markets, support innovation and create new opportunities for more inclusive growth. In the #Philippines, IFAD’s Rural Agroenterprise Partnerships for Inclusive Development and Growth Project (RAPID) is strengthening agricultural value chains to improve rural livelihoods and transform rural economies. Through stronger partnerships across agricultural value chains, RAPID has reached 84,711 small-scale farmers, 876 farmers' organizations and 1,049 micro, small and medium enterprises (MSMEs) – helping connect rural producers and businesses with market opportunities and supporting more inclusive, sustainable growth. By improving access to markets, productive capital, knowledge and technology, RAPID is helping small-scale producers and rural enterprises strengthen their businesses, build resilience and create new opportunities for rural communities. ہدایت کی. وزیراعظم نے الائیڈ بینک کے مجوزہ ایس ایم ای پارک کے قیام کےلئے سرمایہ کاری کے منصوبے کی پزیرائی کی. وزیراعظم نے اپنا گھر ہاؤسنگ سکیم سے مستفید ہونے کے متمنی افراد کے لیے کوائف فراہم کرنے کا عمل مزید آسان کرنے، ہاؤسنگ فنانس کے لیے غیر متنازع ملکیتی دستاویزات (Unencumbered Title Deed) کا حصول آسان بنانے اور ڈیویلپرز فنانس سے متعلق کمیٹی کی سفارشات کو جلد از جلد حتمی شکل دے کر پیش کرنے کی ہدایت کی. اجلاس کو ہاوسنگ، زرعی شعبے اور چھوٹے و درمیانے درجے کے کاروباری اداروں کو قرضوں کی فراہمی کے اعداد وشمار پیش کئے گئے. بریفنگ میں بتایا گیا کہ بینکوں کی جانب سے تینوں ترجیحی شعبوں کے لیے ادارہ جاتی استعداد بڑھائی جا رہی ہے. ڈیویلپرز فنانس کے فروغ کے لیے کام جاری ہے اور اس ضمن میں ایک کمیٹی بھی تشکیل دی جا چکی ہے. وزیراعظم اپنا گھر اسکیم کے تحت اب تک 448 ارب روپے مالیت کے 75 ہزار 198 قرضوں کی منظوری ہوئی ہے ۔ اب تک 14 ہزار افراد کو 76 ارب روپے کے قرضے جاری کیے جا چکے ہیں. رواں سال 125,000 رہائشی یونٹس کے لیے 700 ارب روپے کے قرضوں کی فراہمی کا ہدف رکھا گیا ہے. بریفنگ میں مزید بتایا گیا کہ ہاؤسنگ فنانس کے حوالے سے درخواستوں پر کارروائی کا دورانیہ کم کرکے صرف 15 کاروباری دن تک محدود کر دیا گیا ہے. ہاؤسنگ فنانس کے لیے دستاویزات کی تعداد 25 سے کم کرکے صرف 5 کر دی گئی ہے. زرعی شعبے کے لیے قرضوں کا مجموعی حجم 1352 ارب روپے ہے، جس سے 34 لاکھ 55 ہزار افراد مستفید ہوئے. جون 2027 تک زرعی قرضوں کا حجم 1,500 ارب روپے اور مستفید ہونے والوں کی تعداد 45 لاکھ کا ہدف مقرر ہے. ایس ایم ای شعبے کے 3 لاکھ 52 ہزار سے زائد کاروباری افراد کو 1,137 ارب روپے کے قرضے فراہم کیے جا چکے ہیں. جون 2027 تک ایس ایم ای شعبے کے قرضوں کا حجم 1,500 ارب روپے اور قرض حاصل کرنے والے کاروباری اداروں کی تعداد 5 لاکھ 75 ہزار کا ہدف مقرر ہے. ایس ایم ایز کے لیے نظرثانی شدہ ضوابط اور ہاؤسنگ فنانس کے طریقہ کار کو مزید آسان اور مؤثر بنانے کےلئے اقدامات لئے جارہے ہیں. قرضوں کی فراہمی میں مشترکہ رسک شیئرنگ، سپلائی چین فنانسنگ کے فروغ ، مستند ڈیٹا شیئرنگ اور دیگر جاری اقدامات پر بھی بریفنگ دی گئی. اجلاس میں وفاقی وزراء رانا تنویر حسین، ڈاکٹر مصدق مسعود ملک، عطاء اللہ تارڑ، ریاض حسین پیر زادہ، احد خان چیمہ، شزا فاطمہ خواجہ، وزیراعظم کے مشیر ہارون اختر، وزیر مملکت برائے خزانہ بلال اظہر کیانی ، جے ایس بینک، عسکری بینک، الائیڈ بینک، حبیب میٹرو بینک، بینک آف خیبر اور ایم سی بی اسلامک بینک کے سی ای اوز اور متعلقہ اداروں کے اعلیٰ افسران شریک تھے۔

وزیرِ اعظم محمد شہباز شریف کا قیمتی پتھروں و جواہرات (Gemstones) کے پائلٹ پراجیکٹ کی تیاری میں سست روی اور شعبے کی ترقی کیلئے اقدامات میں تعطل پر اظہار برہمی، ترجیحی بنیادوں پر معینہ مدت کے ساتھ لائحہ عمل مرتب کرکے پیش کرنے کی ہدایت کردی. اجلاس سے گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ قیمتی پتھروں و جواہرات کے شعبے کی ترقی کے حوالے سے اقدامات ترجیح ہیں، کسی قسم کی سست روی قبول نہیں. قیمتی پتھروں کی کان کنی اور انکی تراش خراش سے ویلیو ایڈیشن کا ایک پورا ایکو-سسٹم تیار کیا جائے. قیمتی پتھروں کی غیر معیاری طریقہ کار سے کان کنی اور اسمگلنگ کی وجہ سے ملک کو سالانہ اربوں ڈالر کا نقصان اٹھانا پڑتا ہے. وزیرِ اعظم نے مزید کہا کہ پاکستان کو اللہ رب العزت نے قدرتی وسائل کی دولت سے مالامال کیا ہے. قیمتی پتھروں اور معدنیات کے وسیع ذخائر سے برآمدات میں اضافے کیلئے ترجیحی بنیادوں پر اقدامات اٹھائے جائیں. وزیر اعظم نے ہدایات دیں کہ خطے کے دوسرے ممالک کی طرح قیمتی پتھروں و جواہرات کیلئے برانڈ پاکستان پر کام کریں. ویلیو ایڈیشن کیلئے سینٹرز آف ایکسیلینس کے جلد قیام کا لائحہ عمل مرتب کیا جائے. پائلٹ پراجیکٹس اور قیمتی پتھروں کی ماڈل مائنز کی تعمیر کیلئے تمام تر رکاوٹیں دور کرکے منصوبوں کو جلد مکمل کیا جائے. وزیرِ اعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی زیر صدارت قیمتی پتھروں و جواہرات کے شعبے ترقی اور انکی برامدات میں اضافے کیلئے اقدامات کے حوالے سے جائزہ اجلاس آج اسلام آباد میں منعقد ہوا. اجلاس میں وزیرِ اعظم کو قیمتی پتھروں کی کھوج، تراش خراش اور ان کی ویلیو ایڈیشن کے بعد برآمدات کیلئے تیاری کے پائلٹ پراجیکٹ پر پیش رفت پر تفصیلی بریفنگ دی گئی. اجلاس کو بتایا گیا کہ حسین آباد اسکردو میں سینٹر آف ایکسیلیس منصوبے کیلئے 4.8 کنال زمین منتقل ہو چکی، منصوبے کے لئے فنڈز دستیاب ہیں اور تعمیر پر جلد شروع کر دیا جائیگا. اجلاس کو مزید بتایا گیا کہ آزاد جموں و کشمیر اور اسلام آباد میں منصوبے کیلئے زمین کی نشاندہی کی جاچکی ہے. اسلام آباد میں سینٹر آف ایکسیلینس کی تعمیر تک اسے متبادل جگہ پر مکمل طور پر آپریشنل کر دیا جائیگا. اجلاس کو شعبے کی ترقی کیلئے پالیسی اقدامات پر بھی بریفنگ دی گئی. اجلاس کو بتایا گیا کہ قیمتی پتھروں و جواہرات کے حوالے سے نشاندہی شدہ علاقوں کی جیولاجیکل میپنگ مکمل ہو چکی جس میں گلگت بلتستان، آزاد جموں و کشمیر اور خیبر پختونخوا میں 8 نئے بلاکس کی قیمتی پتھروں کی دریافت کے حوالے سے مزید کام کیلئے نشاندہی کی گئی ہے. اس سال شعبے کی ترقی کے لئے پبلک سیکٹر ڈیولپمنٹ کی مد میں 1 ارب روپے مختص کئے گئے ہیں۔ برآمد کنندگان کی سہولت کے لیے 7 شہروں کے 10 بینکوں کی 80 شاخوں میں ایکسپورٹ فیسیلیٹیشن ڈیسک قائم کیے گئے ہیں۔ وزیرِ اعظم نے آئندہ ہفتے قیمتی پتھروں و جواہرات کیلئے سینٹرز آف ایکسیلینس کے قیام اور شعبے کی ترقی کے حوالے سے اقدامات کا جامع لائحہ عمل مرتب کرکے پیش کرنے کی ہدایت کی. اجلاس میں وفاقی وزراء جام کمال خان، ڈاکٹر مصدق مسعود ملک، احد خان چیمہ، احسن اقبال، عطاء اللہ تارڑ، علی پرویز ملک، مشیر وزیرِ اعظم ہارون اختر، وزیرِ مملکت بلال اظہر کیانی اور متعلقہ اعلی حکام نے شرکت کی.

Advancing India’s capabilities in quantum-secured communications, DRDO successfully configured and tested Quantum Key Distribution(QKD) platform in the live network of the dynamic test ranges at Proof & Experimental Establishment (PXE), Chandipur. This demonstrates the adept use case of QKD to fortify the real-time critical observations & telemetry associated with Artillery and Armoured Weapon tests and evaluation. Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) has been designed and developed under Microelectronic Devices, Computational Systems & Cyber Security (MCC) cluster of DRDO with production partner Taqbit labs and will aptly provide unconditional security added with eavesdropping detection.

War crimes and crimes against humanity are not erased by political narratives, military necessity or passage of time. International law is clear: Those who order, commit, facilitate, or knowingly enable such crimes bear individual criminal responsibility. #JusticeforLamerd Reza Nasri (@RezaNasri1) An Open Letter to @LockheedMartin To James D. Taiclet, Chairman and Chief Executive Officer, and to the Board of Directors. I have just returned from Lamerd, a city of thirty thousand in Iran's Fars province. On 28 February 2026, the opening day of the American and Israeli war on Iran, United States forces fired Precision Strike Missiles built by your corporation into its residential streets, its school and its sports hall. Twenty-one civilians were killed. More than one hundred and seventy were wounded — among them children who will live the rest of their lives without sight, without limbs, or without the use of their spines. The youngest of the dead was Avina Barzegar. She was two. Her photograph is taped above the fragment holes in her family's steel door. I have stood in front of it. Within a month, your corporation signed an agreement to quadruple production of the weapon that did this, reported at some $8.4 billion. I write because the legal consequences of having done so knowingly are more serious than your officers appear to have been advised. What occurred at Lamerd was a war crime. There was no military objective. Under the customary rule reflected in Article 52(2) of Additional Protocol, an object may be attacked only where it effectively contributes to military action and its destruction offers a definite military advantage. In six months, Central Command has identified no such object in Lamerd. It first claimed no American strike occurred within thirty miles of the city. When video made that untenable, it claimed the munition was an Iranian cruise missile, a claim rejected independently by Janes, McKenzie Intelligence, The New York Times and BBC Verify, each identifying the silhouette, the airburst and the fragmentation pattern of one weapon in that theatre. Yours. A denial is not a justification. Where an attacker answers civilian deaths by denying the attack rather than defending the target, it forecloses every defence the law makes available to it. The means were indiscriminate. The PrSM detonates fifteen to twenty metres above ground and disperses tens of thousands of tungsten fragments across a wide area. Investigators counted thousands of fragment impacts along a single 150-metre stretch of one residential street. The casualty pattern is not evidence of a strike gone wrong. It is evidence of the weapon working exactly as designed, in a place where its design guaranteed the result. And the strikes were successive. The first detonated above a sports hall where a girls' volleyball team was training. People ran into the open. The second fell on them. Then a third, then a fourth. Whatever might be argued about the first, nothing explains the rest except a decision taken with knowledge of what the first had just done. A city is not a proving ground. The PrSM had never been used in combat before that day. Lamerd was its debut, and Central Command's commander publicly praised that debut within days. It is sometimes assumed that validating a weapon under operational conditions is a military benefit that can be weighed in the balance. It cannot. The advantage the law requires must be "definite", "concrete and direct" — language chosen precisely to exclude benefits that are speculative, generalised or deferred. Performance data accrues to a production line, not to an attack. It belongs to no part of the balance a commander is permitted to strike. If the rationale was to observe the weapon's effects under live conditions, the civilians of Lamerd were not incidental to the object of the attack. They were the medium on which effectiveness was measured. The contract was made with knowledge. Complicity does not require sharing the perpetrator's purpose. It requires assistance having a substantial effect, furnished with knowledge. That is the standard on which the Hamburg court convicted the suppliers of Zyklon B in 1946; on which the Netherlands convicted Frans van Anraat for supplying chemical precursors to Iraq, holding expressly that the lawful commercial form of the transaction gave him no shelter; and which the French Cour de cassation confirmed reaches corporations in Lafarge. Your original contracts predate Lamerd. The expansion does not. By the time it was signed, the forensic record was public, the official account had collapsed twice, and CENTCOM had itself identified the operation as the weapon's combat debut. A prime contractor does not learn of its munition's first combat use from the newspapers. The expansion was not made in ignorance of how the weapon performed at Lamerd. It was made because of it. Your counsel will know that the corporation is not the principal exposure. Nuremberg did not try I.G. Farben or Krupp; it tried the men who ran them. Van Anraat went to prison as an individual. Officers who authorise continued manufacture and transfer after notice do so in their own names, in a world where Germany, the Netherlands, Belgium, France, Spain, Sweden and others exercise universal jurisdiction over grave breaches. That exposure does not lapse, and it travels. Accordingly: rescind the expansion agreement; suspend production and transfer pending an independent forensic investigation; preserve and disclose the performance data you hold on the Lamerd employment, because it is evidence; and cooperate with any prosecuting authority that opens a file. The answer that these are matters for the government and not the contractor was made at Nuremberg and failed there. A company that builds the weapon, receives the data on what it did to a city of thirty thousand, and then contracts to build four times as many is not a bystander to the decision. Do not repeat the claim that the matter is still under investigation. This is a government that tells its public it can read a name tag from orbit. It closed the Lamerd file in days, by denial, without answering a single question put to it. It has known since the morning of 28 February. It has decided the truth is inconvenient. Your corporation is now being asked whether it has decided the same. Avina Barzegar was two years old. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/RezaNasri1/status/2099166408122798584#m

Election Day is 3 weeks away. As of today, early voting has begun in 15 states. Here are 5 things to know to get you ready for a vote that "could change party control of Congress, and with it, the direction of U.S. politics," according to expert @JamesMLindsay: 1. We already know the winners of 90% of House races and 75% of Senate races, Lindsay notes. Election forecasters rank only about 20 House and just 5 Senate races as toss-ups. “In short, most congressional general elections are uncompetitive, hardly the sign of a healthy, well-functioning democracy,” writes Lindsay. 2. Control of the House of Representatives is the Democrats’ to lose, Lindsay says. "House midterms generally go badly for members of the president’s party. . . . In 2026, the Democrats need a net gain of just 3 seats to retake control of the House. With President Donald Trump’s approval number in the mid-thirties, history suggests that Democrats are a shoe-in to retake control of the House come January 3." 3. A friendly electoral cycle for Senate Republicans has turned difficult. "Unlike the House, Senate midterms elections have not historically functioned as a referendum on the president . . . . Despite these favorable political winds, Trump’s unpopularity, rising fuel prices, and a general sense that life is becoming unaffordable for too many Americans have combined to put a half dozen supposedly safe Republican seats in play," Lindsay argues. 4. Neither the Democrats nor the Republicans have cemented their control of Congress in this century. "If there is one word to summarize Congress in the 21st century, it is 'turnover,'" Lindsay notes. "Party control of the House has changed 4 times since 2000, and party control of the Senate has changed 7 times . . . . Control of one if not both houses of Congress will change after the 2026 vote, a further sign of the country’s inability to forge a stable governing coalition." 5. Election Day is also about state races. "Overlooked in the discussion about the return of divided government to Washington is what will happen in the states," Lindsay writes. "Democrats are hoping that the favorable political winds they are seeing at the national level will also boost their candidates at the state level . . . . If election forecasters are right, Democrats could emerge from Election Day 2026 controlling a majority of governorships and a near majority of state legislatures." Demandamos el decreto que reforma el uso de la fuerza pública en la protesta. Es regresivo e inconstitucional. 1. Solo el Congreso, mediante ley estatutaria, puede fijar los casos en que se limita el derecho a la protesta (art. 37 de la Constitución). Hacerlo por decreto debilita la movilización y la división de poderes. 2. El Decreto 003 de 2021, que el Gobierno de Abelardo modifica, nació de una orden de la Corte Suprema tras los excesos de la fuerza pública en 2019. El Gobierno lo cambió con una consulta de solo 7 días y sin convocar la Mesa Nacional de Garantías. 3. El nuevo decreto convierte el diálogo en una simple “preferencia” y permite saltárselo, también la mediación, incluso cuando no hay violencia. Además, abre la puerta a disolver protestas pacíficas por bloqueos. Esto es un retroceso. 4. La protesta es pacífica, pero también disruptiva. Bloquear una vía no es delito por sí solo (C-742/12), y el Gobierno lo justifica con cifras gremiales que él mismo reconoce como no verificadas. 5. Cuando se debilitan los contrapesos, la protesta pacífica es la herramienta para defender otros derechos: la libre asociación, la educación, la autonomía y la consulta previa. A proud moment for Nepal! 🇳🇵 Today, Nepal has been elected to # UN Human Rights Council for the 2027–2029 term by the UN General Assembly. Nepal previously served two consecutive terms on the Council from 2018 to 2023. Securing 173 out of 180 votes, Nepal received the highest number of votes in its group. We extend our profound appreciation and gratitude to all UN Member States for their enduring trust and confidence placed in Nepal’s steadfast commitment to advancing multilateralism, human rights, international law and a rules-based international system with the UN at its core. We also congratulate Brazil, Burundi, Dominican Republic, Germany, Ghana, Ireland, Japan, Jordan, Kuwait, Moldova, Nigeria, Ukraine, Uruguay and Zambia on their elections to #HRC for 2027-2029. Nepal looks forward to working closely with UN membership and all partners for safeguarding human dignity, inclusion, social justice and equitable development for all, leaving no one behind.

وزیرِ اعظم محمد شہباز شریف نے آج مسلم لیگ (ن) کی پارلیمانی پارٹی سے خطاب کیا۔ وزیراعظم نے کہا کہ خیبر پختونخوا پاکستان کا انتہائی خوبصورت صوبہ ہے اور وہاں کے عوام غیرت مند اور بہادر ہیں جنہوں نے ہمیشہ پاکستان کی ترقی اور خوشحالی کے لیے بھرپور ساتھ دیا اور دہشت گردی کے خلاف جنگ میں عظیم قربانیاں پیش کیں۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ 2017-18 تک پاکستان میں دہشت گردی کا مکمل خاتمہ کر دیا گیا تھا تاہم پاکستان تحریک انصاف کی حکومت آنے پر سوات میں دہشت گرد دوبارہ آنا شروع ہوگئے اور انہیں کھلی چھوٹ دی گئی۔ وزیراعظم نے کہا کہ 2024ء میں خیبر پختونخوا میں دوبارہ حکومت بننے کے بعد گزشتہ ڈھائی سال کے دوران وفاقی حکومت نے صوبائی حکومت کے ساتھ مل کر چلنے کی حتی الامکان کوششیں کیں، سابق وزیراعلیٰ علی امین گنڈاپور سے متعدد ملاقاتیں ہوئیں اور انہیں یقین دلایا گیا کہ ملک کی ترقی اور خوشحالی کا سفر مشترکہ ہے اور دہشت گردی کا مقابلہ کرنا بھی مشترکہ ذمہ داری ہے، نئے وزیراعلیٰ کے انتخاب کے بعد بھی صوبائی حکومت کے ساتھ تعاون کی کوششیں جاری رکھی گئیں۔انہوں نے کہا کہ آج خیبر پختونخوا میں عوام، پولیس اہلکار اور افسران شہید اور اغواء ہو رہے ہیں جبکہ فوج کے افسران اور جوان بھی اپنی جانوں کا نذرانہ پیش کر رہے ہیں، اگر دہشت گردی اور خون خرابے کا مکمل طور پر خاتمہ نہ کیا گیا تو گزشتہ ڈھائی سال کے دوران ملک نے ترقی کا جو سفر طے کیا ہے، اسے جاری رکھنا مشکل ہوگا۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ ماضی کے مسائل اور چیلنجز سے نمٹتے ہوئے ملک آگے بڑھ رہا ہے اور یہ سب ٹیم ورک، مضبوط شراکت داری، خلوص اور سنجیدگی سے ممکن ہوا ہے۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ حکومت کا مقصد غربت اور بے روزگاری کا خاتمہ اور سب سے بڑھ کر پاکستان کے 24 کروڑ عوام کو قرضوں کی زنجیروں سے آزاد کرانا ہے، تاریخ میں ایسی قوموں کی مثالیں موجود ہیں جنہوں نے قرضوں سے نجات حاصل کی، اس لیے پاکستان کے لیے بھی یہ ہدف حاصل کرنا ناممکن نہیں تاہم اس کے لیے محنت، امانت اور دیانت درکار ہے۔وزیراعظم نے کہا کہ اگر کوئی صوبائی حکومت ملک کی ترقی کے سفر کو آگے بڑھانے کے بجائے اسے ختم کرنے کے درپے ہو اور اسے یہ خدشہ ہو کہ ملک نے ترقی کرلی تو اس کی اپنی حیثیت کیا رہ جائے گی تو یہ افسوسناک صورتحال ہے۔ انہوں نے واضح کیا کہ وہ خیبر پختونخوا کے عوام نہیں بلکہ صوبائی حکومت کی بات کر رہے ہیں۔انہوں نے کہا کہ گزشتہ سال اسلام آباد میں ڈی چوک پر ہونے والے دھرنے اور 2013-14 میں کئی ماہ تک جاری رہنے والے احتجاج سب کے سامنے ہیں، 2013ء میں چینی صدر شی جن پنگ کا پاکستان کا دورہ بھی ایسی ہی صورتحال کے باعث موخر ہوا ۔وزیراعظم نے کہا کہ ایسے حالات میں جب ملک کو دہشت گردی کا مقابلہ کرنا ہو، وفاقی حکومت کے ساتھ کھڑے ہونے، افواج پاکستان کا ساتھ دینے، پولیس کو بااختیار بنانے اور انسداد دہشت گردی کے محکمے (سی ٹی ڈی) کو مضبوط کرنے کے بجائے دھرنوں، گالم گلوچ اور دشنام طرازی پر توجہ دی جا رہی ہے۔ انہوں نے کہا کہ حالیہ ہفتوں اور مہینوں کے دوران سابق وزیراعلیٰ نے جس طرح کی باتیں اور دشنام طرازی کی وہ کوئی دشمن بھی نہیں کر سکتا۔انہوں نے کہا کہ دہشت گردی کے خلاف جنگ میں ساتھ دینے کے بجائے افواج پاکستان کے شہداء کے خلاف دشنام طرازی کی جا رہی ہے جبکہ دہشت گردوں کے خلاف کوئی بات کرنے کو نے جواب میں واضح کیا کہ پاکستان وہی ہے تاہم ملک میں تبدیلی آئی ہے اور حکومت کی جانب سے ٹیم ورک کے ذریعے کیے جانے والے اقدامات اس کا نتیجہ ہیں جس پر آئی ایم ایف کی منیجنگ ڈائریکٹر نے کہا کہ پاکستان میں دونالد ترمپ، رییس جمهور ایالات متحده با نشر پیامی در حساب تروت سوشیل خود با اشاره به حملات اخیر حوثی ها بر عربستان سعودی گفت که حوثی ها ممکن این حملات را به اشاره ایران انجام داده باشند. رییس جمهور ترمپ گفت: " "فکر می‌کردم آنان (حوثی‌ها) یک سال پیش درس گرفته بودند، زمانی که به شدت بمباران شان کردیم و پس از آنکه تقاضا کردند، [به حملات] توقف دادیم. آنان برای مدت طولانی خاموش بودند، اما اکنون دوباره ظهور کردند، ممکن به فرمایش ایران - یک کشور در حال ناکامی، با هیچ نیروی بحری، هیچ نیروی هوایی، بدترین اقتصاد جهان و با ۳۰۱ در صد تورم، به بدترین صورت – عربستان سعودی را هدف قرار می‌دهند و هدفمندانه می‌خواهند قیمت نفت را افزایش دهند، شاید پیش از انتخابات در ایالات متحده – این کار خوب نیست. کسی باید برای آنان توضیح دهد من در انتخابات شرکت نمی‌کنم، من از قبل برنده شده ام، آنهم با اختلاف بسیار زیاد، اما پس از انتخابات در آنجا حضور خواهم داشت و هیچ زمانی فراموش نخواهم کرد."

Talarico has a lot of luck, all of it bad.⬇️ Seth Keshel (@RealSKeshel) This is simply not proof of anything. There are many issues with the story on both sides of this issue. On one hand we have a call taking place on Oct 10, the date of supposed discharge, when Talarico was in Austin on Oct 9. That could be a mistake (the employee read the patient file wrong), a system issue feature, or perhaps the wrong person was looked up and there was no Talarico there. Still, it is quite clear the woman was given the name, took time to look it up, and gave the information. So it is natural for this story to take off and for people to want answers. There is no possibility for 100% proof unless it was admitted by Talarico or through the legal process it was discovered. Then the clinic violated its own confirm/deny policy to put out a statement saying he wasn’t receiving treatment from them, and you have Talarico out there mixing his own story up about what kind of medical care he pursued and in which city he did so. So the questions persist. Now today we have the NYT running cover, but with nothing more than “trust us, we saw it.” Can you imagine if the Dems were after Trump for some supposed scandal and he went to the NYT to have them exonerate without evidence shown to the public? Of course you can’t. The very effort to run cover raises even more questions about this issue. Sortor is being accused of using AI; yet no one is accusing the NYT or Talarico campaign of using AI to make security footage with time stamps, or ask if they even exist since we can’t see them. You mean to tell me this issue couldn’t have been extinguished on Oct 8 when the hunt for Talarico began? I fear that we have reached a time in which it is nearly impossible for truth to be discerned. Everything can now be written off as AI and discarded, so long as there is not 100% proof of an act being committed. Caught on video doing something? Had Paxton done the same the media would have funded a manhunt and aired it 24/7. Despite loss, fear, exhaustion and multiple displacements, he kept showing up for his patients. His story reflects the resilience of health workers across Gaza, who carry the same losses as everyone around them while continuing to care for others. Constant exposure to traumatic events has left everyone in Gaza distressed, underscoring need of mental health and psychological support. @WHO and partners, in collaboration with the Ministry of Health, are doing all they can to sustain and strengthen mental health services across Gaza. This includes training health workers, integrating mental health care into health facilities, establishing inpatient and outpatient facilities, provision of medication and ensuring support for health workers. But much more is needed to respond to the scale of the need. WHO calls for: 🔹Protection of health care. 🔹Unimpeded humanitarian access and an expedited flow of aid into Gaza. 🔹Continued support for the health response, which remains underfunded. Today, Zelenskyy, Starmer, Macron, and Merz meet in London. The format itself is worth welcoming, even if the EU has once again been left on the sidelines. The real question is what mindset the E3 brings to the table. Zelenskyy set the tone with his open letter to Putin. While his European partners likely share its substance, they are unlikely to be ready to openly put their signatures beneath it. But they do see that Russia is not looking for middle ground. It is set on war. Seeking a balanced compromise with an aggressor committed to conquest is not diplomacy. It is self-deception. The predecessors of today’s leaders understood this well. Symbolically, eighty-five years ago, London hosted another gathering. In June 1941, representatives of fourteen Allied governments and liberation movements met there to unite against Nazism. The final London Declaration was not about ending a war. It was about uniting those willing to win it and shape the peace that followed. One can only hope today’s meeting is guided by the same logic. Europe’s prosperity depends on its security. Europe’s security depends on Ukraine. It is time to turn that truth into effective policy. And fast.

وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف سے پاکستان مسلم لیگ (ق)، بلوچستان عوامی پارٹی، استحکام پاکستان پارٹی اور مسلم لیگ (ضیاء) کے پارلیمانی وفد کی ملاقات آج اسلام آباد میں ہوئی. وفد میں بلوچستان عوامی پارٹی (BAP) کے صدر اور وفاقی وزیر خالد مگسی، سابق چیئرمین سینیٹ اور ایم پی اے صادق سنجرانی، سینیٹرز منظور کاکڑ، عبدالقادر بلوچ، دنیش کمار، ثمینہ ممتاز زہری سابق سینیٹر فدا محمد خان، پاکستان مسلم لیگ (ق) کے صدر اور وفاقی وزیر چوہدری سالک حسین , اراکین قومی اسمبلی محمد الیاس چوہدری اور محترمہ فرح خان، استحکام پاکستان پارٹی کے وزیر مملکت عون ثقلین عباس، اراکین قومی اسمبلی گل اصغر خان اور منزہ حسن، پی ایم ایل (ضیا) کے صدر اور ممبر قومی اسمبلی محمد اعجاز الحق شامل تھے وزیراعظم نے وفد کو صوبہء خیبر پختونخوا کی صورتحال پر اعتماد میں لیا. گفتگو کرتے ہوئے وزیرِ اعظم نے کہا کہ خیبر پختونخوا میں امن و امان کی صورتحال بہتر بنانے، معیشت کی بہتری اور دہشت گردی کے خاتمے کے لیے گورنر کی معاونت کے لئے غیر جانب دار ٹیکنوکریٹ ایڈوائزری کونسل قائم کی گئی ہے. خیبر پختونخوا میں پی ٹی آئی حکومت کے طرزِ عمل اور دہشت گردی کے خلاف دو ٹوک موقف کے اجتناب سے پاکستان کی ترقی کرتی معیشت کو خطرات لاحق تھے. وفاقی کابینہ نے باہمی مشاورت سے آئین کے آرٹیکل 232 اور 234 کے تحت آئینی اقدامات کا فیصلہ کیا. خیبر پختونخوا میں پاکستان تحریک انصاف کی حکومت نے دہشت گردی کی واضح الفاظ میں مذمت نہیں کی اور نہ ہی دہشت گردوں کے خلاف کوئی بھرپور کاروائی کی. وزیرِ اعظم نے مزید کہا کہ گزشتہ کئی سالوں سے خیبر پختونخوا میں پاک افواج، سیکیورٹی فورسز اور پولیس کے کئی اہلکاروں نے جام شہادت نوش کیا اور مادر وطن کی حفاظت کی خاطر اپنی جانوں کا نذرانہ پیش کیا. پچھلے 13 سالوں میں پاکستان تحریک انصاف اور خیبر پختونخوا کی صوبائی حکومت نے نا ہی عوامی فلاح و بہبود کے لئے کام کیا اور نا ہی عوام کی جان و مال کی حفاظت کے لئے خاطر خواہ اقدامات کئے، صرف انتشار کا راستہ اپنایا گیا. وفاقی حکومت نے خیبر پختونخوا کو دہشت گردی کے خاتمے کے لیے NFC کے تحت 800 ارب روپے سے زائد فنڈز فراہم کیے. خیبر پختونخوا حکومت دہشت گردی کے خلاف جنگ کے لیے کاؤنٹر ٹیررازم ڈیپارٹمنٹ کی استعداد کار بڑھانے اور سیف سٹیز کے قیام کے لیے مؤثر اقدامات کرنے میں ناکام رہی. پارلیمانی وفد نے وزیرِ اعظم کو یقین دہانی کروائی کہ اتحادی جماعتیں موجودہ صورتحال میں وفاقی حکومت کے ساتھ کھڑی ہیں. اتحادی جماعتوں کے پارلیمانی وفد نے مشکل حالات میں ملک کی قیادت اور رہنمائی کرنے پر وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی قیادت کو خراجِ تحسین پیش کیا. وفد کے ارکان نے اظہار خیال کرتے ہوئے کہا کہ خیبر پختونخوا کے عوام گزشتہ 13 سال سے پی ٹی آئی کی حکومت کے دور میں صحت، تعلیم اور انفراسٹرکچر کے شعبوں میں ترقی سے محروم رہے. وفاقی حکومت کے تعاون سے خیبر پختونخوا میں بھی ملک کے دیگر حصوں کی طرح ترقی اور خوشحالی کا سفر آگے بڑھے گا. ملاقات میں نائب وزیراعظم و وزیر خارجہ محمد اسحاق ڈار، وزیر دفاع خواجہ محمد آصف، وفاقی وزیر قانون و انصاف اعظم نذیر تارڑ، وفاقی وزیر پارلیمانی امور ڈاکٹر طارق فضل چوہدری اور وزیراعظم کے مشیر برائے سیاسی امور و بین الصوبائی روابط رانا ثناء اللہ بھی موجود تھے۔ Video

I am a member of the Norwegian Nobel Committee. There are five of us. Five people, appointed by a parliament most of the planet could not find on a map, who decide, once a year, which human being the world has agreed to call good. I know. I know. I think about it on the tram. We meet in a building on Henrik Ibsens gate, a street named after a man who wrote almost exclusively about people discovering they are frauds, which nobody on the committee finds funny except me. There is a room with a long table and the portraits of the dead laureates looking down, Mandela, the Dalai Lama, a great many earnest men in spectacles, and one portrait we do not discuss, which is Kissinger, 1973, awarded while the bombs were still falling, after which two of our predecessors resigned and the satirist Tom Lehrer said political satire was now obsolete. We keep him on the wall. A reminder. Every family has the uncle. It is October in Oslo, which means the sun gives up around four in the afternoon like a civil servant, and it rains the particular Norwegian rain that isn’t quite falling, just hanging there, judging you. I arrive with wet shoes. I always arrive with wet shoes. There is coffee, because this is Norway and there is always coffee, we drink more of it per person than almost anyone alive, and someone’s wife has sent kanelboller, the cinnamon buns, and we sit, five Norwegians, damp, caffeinated, sugared, and we decide the moral standing of the entire species. Let me tell you how it actually works, because the world imagines a cathedral and it is, I promise you, a book club with a mandate. 287 nominations this year. 208 people, 79 organizations. Anyone can nominate, that’s the secret nobody understands: a professor, a parliamentarian, a former laureate, so the “nominee” list is meaningless, it’s a suggestion box, and every autumn some congressman nominates his own golden retriever and the press writes “SHORTLISTED.” Nobody is shortlisted. There is no short list the public ever sees. There is us, and the coffee, and the rain, and the portraits, and a Norwegian stubbornness that is older than the prize itself. We read reports. The institute’s advisers write them, thick dull documents, and we argue. Our chairman told the BBC once that in the final meeting “there is a high temperature.” High temperature, for a Norwegian, means someone slightly raised an eyebrow and then apologized for it. We don’t do high temperature. We do a long silence, and then Kristin says “well,” and everyone knows exactly what “well” meant, and it’s settled. That’s our shouting. “Well.” You’d have to be raised here to hear the violence in it. Now. This year. I will not say the name, because we never say the name, but you know the name. A certain head of state wanted this prize the way a child wants a thing in a shop window, which is to say loudly, and in public, and with the full belief that wanting it was itself the argument. He said he deserved it. He said he’d ended eight wars, a number that grew most times he said it, like a fish. He had other heads of state phone us. Israel’s prime minister posted it on the internet, “Give him the Nobel.” The leaders of Cambodia and Pakistan announced they’d nominated him, as though announcing it were part of it, as though we tally mentions. A man flew around the globe collecting endorsements for a Norwegian committee the way you’d collect signatures for a petition to the council about a noisy dog. And here, uff da, is the detail I treasure, the one that makes me smile into my coffee. The nomination deadline is the 31st of January. He took office on the 20th. So for all the phone calls, all the posts, all the gilded lobbying, the only nominations that could possibly count for this year’s prize were filed in the first eleven days of his term, before he had, by his own arithmetic, ended a single one of the eight wars. He campaigned all year for a prize whose window had shut while he was still hanging up his coat. We didn’t have to reject him. The calendar did. We just watched. Norwegians are very good at watching. We have long winters. People think we sit there weighing his deeds. We don’t. That’s the thing I can’t make the world understand. We’re not grading his homework. We don’t owe anyone the prize for a ceasefire, however real, however loud the announcement. “He made peace” is not a sentence that ends in a medal, the way he believes it does, the way he believes every good thing ends in his name on it. The will of a dead Swede says the prize goes to whoever did the most for fraternity between nations. A dead Swede, I should add, who made his entire fortune inventing dynamite and selling arms, and spent his last years horrified at his own obituary, which called him a merchant of death, and so bought his way to immortality as a man of peace. The whole prize is one guilty arms dealer’s attempt to launder his name. We are, all of us, administering a dead man’s public relations. I find this clarifying. It keeps me humble. It should keep everyone humble, and it keeps, by my count, no one humble at all. So who did we give it to? An eighty-five-year-old woman. A judge. Born in Durban, under apartheid, granddaughter of a Tamil man who came to South Africa as indentured labor, a bus driver’s daughter from the poor Indian quarter, who became the first non-white woman to run a law practice in her province, who defended Mandela’s people when defending them was dangerous, who sat on the Rwanda tribunal and the court at the Hague, and who, at eighty-five, is right now a judge weighing whether a genocide is a genocide. When we told the world, our chairman said the rule of law “underpins the system we have set up to ensure peace,” and that “peace requires justice.” She wasn’t even in Oslo. She was in Nuremberg. In courtroom 600. The actual room where they tried the Nazis. You cannot stage that. God staged that, and God, it turns out, is a better satirist than any of us. She did not phone us. She did not post. No prime minister demanded it for her on the internet. She had, as far as our deliberations are concerned, the one qualification the loud man could never manufacture, which is that she wanted the work and not the medal. The medal finds those people. It flees the ones who chase it. This is not a rule we wrote. It’s just the only pattern the hundred-odd years of our mistakes has ever shown. The reaction from across the ocean was immediate. His spokesman posted that we “place politics over peace.” Ja. Perhaps. We’re five damp pensioners in a rainy city; of course it’s political, it was always political, it was political when we gave it to a sitting American president nine months into his first term for the promise of things he had not yet done, and we have been quietly embarrassed about that one for fifteen years, so believe me, we had a particular reason this year to prefer a woman with fifty years of verdicts behind her over a man with eight wars in front of him and a deadline already behind him. Here is what he will never understand, the thing I’d tell him on the tram if he ever took one. He said that despite Afghanistan’s negligible contribution to greenhouse gas emissions, the country has suffered significant losses from the impacts of climate change, including floods, earthquakes, and droughts. The Deputy Prime Minister for Economic Affairs emphasized that Afghanistan should have equitable access to international financial and technical assistance. Delighted to inaugurate the exhibition “Nirāmayāta: Healing and Wellbeing in South Asian Texts and Practices” at @IIC_Delhi today. In my remarks on the occasion, highlighted: ✅ That ‘Nirāmayāta’ is an exploration of a civilizational understanding of the relationship between individual, society & the natural world. ✅ The saṃhitās represent an important milestone in the systematization of traditional knowledge on health that can be studied, taught & transmitted across generations. ✅ The history of healing in the Subcontinent ranges from Vedic hymns & Buddhist monastic traditions to specialized texts on surgery, pharmacology & therapeutics. ✅ Medical knowledge in the Subcontinent travelled across linguistic, geographical & cultural boundaries, growing through experience, exchange and the accumulation of insights across societies. ✅ The breadth of questions examined on health went beyond curing an ailment, reflecting a comprehensive understanding of human wellbeing. ✅ Our traditional knowledge can provide valuable perspectives for contemporary inquiry, identifying these possibilities through credible research. ✅ There is need to recognize the contributions of people like vaidyas, surgeons, hakims, monks, and herbalists who preserved and passed the knowledge on to future generations. ✅ The task before us is to preserve these materials and to make them meaningful to contemporary audiences through digitization, use of AI, cataloguing, scholarly collaboration & public exhibitions. ✅ This endeavor is also part of a larger effort to recover and communicate our civilizational inheritance, in an era where economic and political rebalancing is being followed by a cultural one. ✅ In a world which is undergoing profound change, the preservation of manuscripts is an investment in our intellectual resources, since India’s progress requires technology and tradition to walk together: Vikas Bhi, Virasat Bhi.

I spent 15+ years investigating Russian secret services and organized crime. I know people who served with Putin in the KGB and sat in on his deals with St. Petersburg crime bosses. So let me explain the "diesel deal" the way they would — in gangster slang. Because that's the language Putin actually thinks in. First, the facts. Putin just raised Russia's 2027 military budget by 27% to a record 17.1 trillion rubles — about $203 billion. Who budgets that kind of money for a war they're about to end? The FT reported yesterday that Western intelligence has warned the heads of European defense companies that Russia is plotting to assassinate them. Since September, Tusk, Macron and the intelligence services of Poland, Czechia, Latvia, Belgium, France and Denmark have all warned that Russian hybrid attacks — including drone and missile strikes — will intensify in the coming months. None of this looks like a country preparing for peace. Who actually benefits? 🇺🇸 What the US gets: Every serious analysis I've read says the announced volumes won't move American diesel prices. This is a PR move for Trump before the midterms — a story about prices that will "very, very soon" come down once his friend Vladimir's tankers reach US shores, plus the chance to claim he ended another war (I've lost count). The only US "benefit" is Trump's rating. 🇷🇺 What Russia gets: billions of dollars to keep funding its genocidal war against Ukrainians. Sanctions relief. A demonstration of power to the rest of the world. A deeper rift between the US and its European allies. And a real chance to disrupt US weapons and intelligence flowing to Ukraine. So what is Putin's actual goal? Trump's disapproval is at record highs and polls show his party will most likely loose midterm elections. In less than a month his power will be badly weakened. Why would Putin sign a long-term peace deal with a lame duck whose signature will soon be scrutinized at best and annulled at worst? He wouldn't. And here's where the slang comes in. In the eyes of Putin and his siloviki, Trump is a baryga — a greedy, unscrupulous businessman who puts profit above law and principle. Gangsters despise barygas, but they love using them. The goal is always to turn a baryga into a lokh — a mark, an outsider who doesn't understand the rules of the underworld and gets played to serve the gang's interests. By signing the diesel deal, Putin plays two scenarios at once: A) The deal miraculously helps his lokh keep power — great. B) The deal changes nothing, the baryga loses the midterms — but by then it has already done its job: inflamed US political tensions and acted as arson inside the American system. Putin knows that the majority of Americans support Ukraine. He knows that by signing, Trump draws unprecedented criticism, including from his own party. And he knows a baryga won't give up power easily, because he will have to answer for everything he did in office — this deal included. That's classic gangster/secret-service method: tie a man to your organization, make him a partner in your crimes, so he can't walk away. Pouring more oil — diesel, in this case — onto the most explosive fault lines of American politics, raising the stakes for Trump and pushing him past the point of no return serves Putin far better than a peace deal that could be voided within months. Remember: Putin's goal in the West is chaos, not peace.

وزیراعظم محمد شہباز شریف کی زیرِ صدارت سمیڈا (SMEDA) کے حوالے سے اجلاس آج اسلام آباد میں منعقد ہوا. وزیراعظم نے کہا ہے کہ کاروباری طبقہ کسی بھی ملک کی معیشت میں ریڑھ کی ہڈی کی حیثیت رکھتا ہے، جبکہ پاکستان میں چھوٹے اور درمیانے درجے کے کاروبار (ایس ایم ایز) میں ملکی معیشت کو فروغ دینے کی بے پناہ صلاحیت موجود ہے۔ وزیراعظم نے کہا کہ سمیڈا میں جاری اصلاحات کا محور چھوٹے اور درمیانے درجے کے کاروباری افراد کو بااختیار بنانا ہے۔ وزیراعظم نے کہا کہ پسماندہ علاقوں کے عوام کو بااختیار بنانے سے ان علاقوں سے بڑے شہروں کی جانب نقل مکانی میں کمی آئے گی اور ملک کی مجموعی ترقی کو فروغ ملے گا۔ پسماندہ علاقوں سے تعلق رکھنے والے افراد کو مختلف شعبوں میں کاروبار قائم کرنے کے مواقع فراہم کرنا ان علاقوں کی ترقی اور خوشحالی کے لیے مفید ثابت ہوگا۔ وزیراعظم نے ہدایت کی کہ سمیڈا زیادہ سے زیادہ افراد کو کاروبار کے لیے قرضوں کے حصول کے طریقہ کار سے آگاہ کرنے کے لیے جامع لائحہ عمل مرتب کرے اور عوام میں کاروباری سرگرمیوں کے فروغ کے حوالے سے شعور اجاگر کرنے کے لیے مؤثر اقدامات کرے۔ وزیراعظم نے ہدایت کی کہ مختلف شعبوں میں چھوٹے اور درمیانے درجے کے کاروبار کے قیام کے لیے فیزیبلٹی اسٹڈیز شعبہ جات کے ماہرین سے تیار کروائی جائیں اور انہیں مقامی زبانوں میں بھی دستیاب بنایا جائے تاکہ ملک بھر کے خواہش مند کاروباری افراد ان سے بھرپور استفادہ کر سکیں. وزیراعظم نے چھوٹے اور درمیانے درجے کے کاروباری افراد کے لیے قرضوں کی مجموعی مالیت 2028 تک 1.1 ٹریلین روپے سے بڑھا کر 2.2 ٹریلین روپے کرنے کی ہدایت کی۔ اجلاس میں وزیراعظم کو سمیڈا میں جاری اصلاحات اور چھوٹے و درمیانے درجے کے کاروبار کے فروغ کے لیے کیے جانے والے اقدامات پر بریفنگ دی گئی۔ بریفنگ میں بتایا گیا کہ سمیڈا کو ایک مرکزی پلیٹ فارم میں تبدیل کیا جا رہا ہے، جو چھوٹے اور درمیانے درجے کے کاروبار قائم کرنے کے خواہش مند افراد کو تربیت فراہم کرنے اور کاروبار کے لیے مالی معاونت کے حصول کی غرض سے بینکوں سے رابطے میں سہولت فراہم کرے گا۔ بریفنگ میں بتایا گیا کہ ایس ایم ای شعبے سے وابستہ افراد تک مؤثر رسائی یقینی بنانے کے لیے ملک بھر میں سمیڈا کے دفاتر قائم کیے جا رہے ہیں۔ شہریوں کی سہولت کے لیے مصنوعی ذہانت (اے آئی) پر مبنی ہیلپ لائن قائم کی جا رہی ہے، جس کے ذریعے لوگوں کو مقامی زبانوں میں معلومات اور رہنمائی فراہم کی جائے گی۔ بریفنگ میں بتایا گیا کہ عالمی ای کامرس کمپنی علی بابا اور سمیڈا کے درمیان مفاہمت کی یادداشت پر دستخط ہو چکے ہیں، جس کے تحت دو سال کے عرصے میں دس ہزار چھوٹے اور درمیانے درجے کے کاروباری اداروں (ایس ایم ایز) کو تربیت فراہم کی جائے گی۔ ایس ایم ای ڈیجیٹل پورٹل کو مزید مؤثر اور کاروباری افراد کے لیے سہل بنانے کے لیے اصلاحات جاری ہیں۔ اجلاس میں وفاقی وزراء رانا تنویر حسین، جام کمال خان، ڈاکٹر مصدق مسعود ملک، احد خان چیمہ، عطاء اللہ تارڑ اور چوہدری سالک حسین، وزیر مملکت برائے خزانہ بلال اظہر کیانی، وزیراعظم کے مشیر ہارون اختر، چیئرمین پرائم منسٹر یوتھ پروگرام رانا مشہود احمد خان اور متعلقہ اداروں کے اعلیٰ حکام نے شرکت کی۔ Video

As a father and grandfather, I want the same for every girl as I want for my own daughters and granddaughters: to grow up healthy, safe, and free to pursue their dreams. But the reality for millions of girls is very different. Every year, around 21 million adolescent girls become pregnant in low- and middle-income countries. One in four girls who have been in a relationship experiences physical or sexual violence from a partner. And many girls still miss out on vaccines that could protect them from cervical cancer later in life. These are not just statistics. Behind every number is a girl whose health, choices and future are at stake. This #DayOfTheGirl, let’s commit to give every girl the chance to live a healthy life and fulfil her potential. No exceptions.

I have to monitor them for my dogs, they go crazy with so many commercials. And now with a newborn, can definitely see the challenge in these other types of commercials too. Jimmy Spencer (@JimmySpencer) My 7-year-old son can’t watch sports with me anymore. Not because of the games, but because of the commercials. The horror movie trailers are the worst. The terrifying imagery can send him into a spiral of anxiety that lasts well beyond the 30-second ad. These are images his young mind simply isn’t ready to process. We talk a lot about mental health in this country, especially in sports. Yet between the relentless gambling ads, alcohol promotions and genuinely disturbing horror trailers, I’ve reached a point where watching an MLB or NFL game with my kids requires me to monitor every commercial break. I love sports. I work in sports. Some of my favorite childhood memories were made watching games with my family. I want that for my sons. I wish we could exercise better judgment about what we’re putting in front of families during sporting events. Sports should bring generations together. Instead, I’m increasingly forced to treat game day like an adults-only event. Something feels very wrong about that. — http://nitter.perennialte.ch/JimmySpencer/status/2108282182267711972#m

Is Britain's welfare system helping people or holding them back?⁠ ⁠ About two years ago I met Gavin, a taxi driver who was trying to come off sickness benefit. He had fully recovered from a heart operation and no longer needed the support, but was told he could not sign himself off and needed to wait to be reassessed. And, until he was, he had no choice but to keep taking the money.⁠ ⁠ Today, we can reveal why: reassessments stopped in lockdown and were never properly restarted. Some 1.8 million claimants have been waiting for an average of two years. One has been waiting for 16 years. Ok guys, I’ve been looking into Malala Yousafzai’s charity, the Malala Fund and I have some questions. According to its 2024–2025 financial reports: Revenue: $16.48 MILLION Expenses: $23.34 MILLION Net assets: $42.97 MILLION That means the charity spent approximately $6.86 MILLION MORE than it brought in‼️ And then there are the executive compensation figures: CEO: Approximately $372,000 Chief Adviser: Approximately $320,000 COO: Approximately $241,000 The charity’s tax filings also disclose FIRST CLASS or PRIVATE travel for officers or key employees. ✈️ WTF?! But here’s what I’d like to know: How much of that $18.94 MILLION in program spending actually reaches girls and local educational organizations? How much goes toward salaries, consultants, advocacy campaigns, and travel? What measurable educational results can donors independently verify? And why did a charity with $16.48 million in annual revenue spend over $23 million that year?!? 🤯 When you’re raising millions in the name of educating vulnerable girls, I don’t think asking where the money goes is unreasonable. Charity should be about the cause, not the celebrity attached to it. It now makes sense why Malala looked so comfortable dining at Claridge’s.
